workflow_steps.objective: Define the line's commercial goal, audience, scope, sales channels, budget, schedule, approval owner, success criteria, supplied artwork and unresolved constraints.

Compare audience demand, suitable merchandise categories, competitor positioning, price bands, production routes and fulfilment implications without treating provisional vendor information as confirmed.
Establish product-selection and design criteria covering artwork fidelity, usefulness, differentiation, target margin, production simplicity, quality, sustainability and shipping practicality.
Create a provisional product and SKU architecture, including formats, variants, dimensions, artwork placements, required content and channel-specific asset needs.
Develop meaningfully different merchandise-line directions that vary product mix, artwork treatment, colour strategy and commercial positioning.
Compare directions against the agreed criteria and obtain explicit client approval for one product mix and creative direction before detailed development.
Produce representative samples or proofs and test artwork reproduction, materials, sizing, durability, usability, packaging fit, shipping practicality and perceived value.
Resolve documented prototype and stakeholder feedback while retaining approved product and creative decisions.
Document a repeatable making, quality-control, inventory or made-to-order, packing, fulfilment, returns and replenishment workflow based on confirmed suppliers and successful tests.
Apply the approved direction consistently across the agreed merchandise family, SKU variants, mockups and sales-channel content templates.
Prepare supplier-specific artwork masters, colour instructions, placement files, SKU specifications and export packages only after technical requirements are confirmed.
Validate and hand off the approved merchandise system, production documentation, SKU matrix, mockups, photography and ecommerce assets with versioning and usage guidance.

missing_inputs: Production-ready artwork files, dimensions, colour information and acceptable cropping or adaptation rules
Confirmation of artwork ownership, merchandise rights and any required third-party releases
Target customers, intended positioning and evidence or hypotheses about demand
Preferred or prohibited product categories and the desired number of products, variants and sizes
Launch budget, sample budget, target retail prices, margin requirements and acceptable inventory risk
Sales channels, launch regions, currencies and platform-specific image, copy and SKU requirements
Chosen production and fulfilment model, such as in-house, local maker, small batch or print-on-demand
Supplier capabilities and specifications, including materials, print methods, templates, printable areas, tolerances, colour profiles, minimum quantities, costs and lead times
Quality, durability, sustainability, accessibility and regulatory requirements
Packing, storage, shipping, tracking, returns, damaged-goods and customer-support requirements
Brand assets, product naming conventions, tone of voice and required product-page copy
Launch schedule, approval stakeholders and criteria for accepting prototypes
Availability of final samples, photography location, models or props, shot list and image usage rights
assumptions: The scope is one cohesive small launch line, but no product or SKU count is fixed until commercial and production inputs are confirmed.
The illustrator's existing artistic identity will be retained; creation of a new brand identity is outside scope unless separately approved.
Product categories and manufacturing methods remain provisional and will be selected through agreed criteria rather than presumed factory capabilities.
A human client or rights holder will approve the selected direction, prototypes and final production package.
At least one representative physical sample or supplier proof will be reviewed before production ordering or sales publication.
Photography and ecommerce content will be finalized only after products, samples and sales-channel specifications are confirmed.
The process model will distinguish confirmed supplier instructions from internal recommendations and unresolved decisions.
stop_conditions: Do not finalize the product mix or SKU count until audience, channel, budget, pricing and inventory-risk constraints are approved.
Do not adapt or commercialize artwork until merchandise rights and permitted modifications are confirmed.
Do not promise materials, print quality, costs, minimum quantities or lead times without written supplier information.
Do not prepare final production masters until the selected supplier provides templates, printable areas, tolerances, colour requirements and export specifications.
Do not approve a production run until representative samples or proofs pass documented artwork, material, sizing, durability and quality checks.
Do not activate fulfilment until stock ownership, packing standards, shipping rates, tracking, returns, damaged-goods handling and responsible parties are defined.
Do not create final product photography without approved physical samples and confirmed image requirements.
Do not publish sales listings until approved pricing, SKU data, inventory status, product claims, images, copy, shipping terms and applicable legal information are complete.
rationale: The workflow moves from commercial definition and evidence-based product selection through explicit direction approval, physical validation and refinement. It then converts the validated line into a repeatable operating process, supplier-specific production files and channel-ready sales assets while preserving gates for rights, factory specifications, quality and fulfilment information that the brief does not supply.
